subject: Pilot eval design + scoring rubric for ClearPoint triage assistant
messages:
From: Sarah Mehta <sarah@clearpointhealth.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: pete.tang@clearpointhealth.com
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — triage assistant pilot

Thanks for the call earlier, Jasmine — quick recap and the things we need to move to an internal greenlight. High level: we want a short pilot (3 weeks) to validate model accuracy on our clinical triage intents and ensure hallucination rate is below our threshold.

What we can provide now:
- ~2k de-identified triage transcripts (CSV) with columns: case_id, patient_text, triage_label, severity_score, notes.
- A small human-annotated holdout (300 rows) for scoring.

Open questions we discussed:
- Which Redwood model(s) you recommend for throughput & cost trade-offs?
- Scoring rubric specifics (how you’ll compute hallucination rate / false positive triage).
- Security and retention (SOC2 evidence, how long logs are stored during pilot).

Next steps I need from you this week:
1) Suggested model shortlist and expected token-latency numbers for our average transcript (~120 tokens).
2) A one-page evaluation plan with dataset format, scoring metrics, and acceptance criteria we can share with procurement.
3) A stub S3 upload path + minimal ingestion checklist so our data team can push a sample CSV.

Thanks — Sarah
Sarah Mehta
Director, Clinical Platforms
ClearPoint Health

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Mehta <sarah@clearpointhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot eval design + scoring rubric for ClearPoint triage assistant

Sarah — great to meet you and the team today. Below is a concise plan we can hand to your procurement and data teams. I attached a sample dataset schema CSV, the pilot scoring rubric, and a prompt bank draft.

Summary of recommendations (shortlist):
- Redwood-moderato-7B-q4: Best balance of accuracy and cost for intent/triage classification. Expected median token latency ~95ms for 120-token requests when served on dedicated capacity.
- Redwood-xl-13B (float16): Higher accuracy, slower median token latency ~160ms; recommended only if sensitivity to mis-triage is critical.
- fallback: Open-variant-7B-q4 - good for cost optimization if we need an inexpensive baseline.

Evaluation plan (one-page highlights):
- Dataset format: CSV with header row, UTF-8. Required fields: case_id, patient_text, gold_triage_label, severity_score (0-5), notes. Optional: encounter_type, anonymized_patient_age_group. See attached clearpoint_eval_dataset_schema.csv.
- Split: we’ll use 80/10/10 for train/dev/test internally; you’ll provide the 300-row human-annotated holdout as the test set.
- Metrics: accuracy (triage_label), macro F1 across labels, weighted F1 for high-severity classes, hallucination rate (percentage of responses with unsupported clinical assertions as judged by labelers), top-1 label precision for red/urgent classes.
- Acceptance criteria (pilot):
  - Macro F1 >= 0.78 OR weighted F1 >= 0.82 for severe classes; AND
  - Hallucination rate <= 3% on the holdout; AND
  - Median per-request latency <= 250ms (hosted/dedicated SLO).

Scoring and human review workflow:
- We will run automated scoring on your holdout and then provide a web-based scorer view for your clinicians to adjudicate edge cases (~300 rows). Adjudications update final metrics.
- Hallucination sampling: we’ll surface 100 model responses flagged by our QA classifier for manual review.

Security & ops notes:
- Pilot runs on Redwood Dedicated (isolated tenants). We retain logs for pilot-only at your requested retention; default is 30 days. SOC2 report + data handling addendum available — requesting your procurement team contact lauren_bishop@redwood.com for formal evidence.

Immediate next actions (this week):
1) Your data upload: provide a sample CSV to the S3 path below (we can create a presigned link if you prefer).
2) Confirm which model(s) you want in the shortlist for the pilot.
3) Procurement: connect with Lauren for SOC2 + DPA follow-up.

Operational stubs (Ben will follow up with exact schema and S3 prefix).

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Mehta <sarah@clearpointhealth.com>, jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot eval design + scoring rubric for ClearPoint triage assistant

Sarah — quick ops note on the ingest and scorer format so your data team has concrete steps.

S3 ingest (preferred):
- We’ll provision a presigned S3 folder for you. File format: CSV, comma-delimited, no Excel formatting. Filename convention: clearpoint_pilot_<YYYYMMDD>_v1.csv
- Minimum sample: 300 rows for test (we’ll accept larger sets). Please remove PHI per our de-ident guidance.

Required columns (CSV):
- case_id (string)
- patient_text (string)
- gold_triage_label (one of: no_action, home_care, urgent_outpatient, urgent_immediate)
- severity_score (0-5 integer)
- annotator_notes (optional)

Scorer UI: we’ll pass you a link to the temporary scorer application where clinicians can mark: correct/incorrect, hallucination_flag (yes/no), severity_misclass (yes/no), comments. Export will be CSV with adjudications.

Sample schema attached as clearpoint_eval_dataset_schema.csv. I also attached a compact scoring rubric (pilot_scoring_rubric.pdf) that maps adjudication flags to metric calculations.

We’ll also run a small baseline run on Redwood-moderato-7B-q4 to show expected performance within 48 hours of receiving the sample. If you want the higher-accuracy Redwood-xl-13B run in the pilot, confirm now so we reserve capacity for the first week.

Ben Carter
Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Mehta <sarah@clearpointhealth.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: pete.tang@clearpointhealth.com, procurement@clearpointhealth.com
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot eval design + scoring rubric for ClearPoint triage assistant

Thanks — that format looks good. Two quick asks before we upload:
1) Can you confirm data retention for pilot logs (we prefer 14 days for temporary logs and hashed storage beyond that).
2) We’ll take Redwood-moderato-7B-q4 as the baseline. Can you reserve one run of Redwood-xl-13B for week 1? We can decide by Friday whether to keep it.

If we get the presigned S3 path today, our data engineer will push a 500-row sample later today. Once you run the baseline, can you share the initial metrics + a link to the scorer UI so our clinicians can start adjudicating?

Sarah
